fact: Civil servants who had not validated their biometric physical check in the SIGRH payroll and HR system had to produce papers including the carte Nina, under a grace period from 8 September 2025 extended to 30 January 2026 (L'Essor).
Mali launched on 10 February 2026 two online platforms, for the criminal record and the nationality certificate, where citizens apply using their NINA and civil-status details (Maliweb).

Decree 2023-0679 of 16 November 2023 makes identification of all state and local civil servants compulsory, matching each agent's data against the biometric RAVEC data, with unidentified agents struck from the payroll file.

Mali's Council of Ministers adopted a draft decree on 8 November 2023 for identifying State and local-government civil servants under an integrated human resources management system that incorporates the biometric data of the civil-status census RAVEC, per Le Sursaut.

fact: The telecoms regulator AMRTP, in a communique of 29 July 2025, required mobile operators to sell no SIM card without a valid identity document carrying the NINA and to give subscribers a way to check the numbers registered against their NINA.

Telecom operators identify SIM card subscribers with their NINA data, and the regulator AMRTP instructed all licensed operators to give subscribers a means to check the phone numbers linked to their NINA, after fraudulent registrations came to light.
AMRTP's communique of 4 November 2024 requires mobile subscribers to identify their SIM cards through the NINA national ID number by 15 December 2024 or have lines deactivated.

Mali's telecoms regulator AMRTP decided that mobile operators identify SIM cards on presentation of the national identification number (NINA) from 1 February 2023, and Orange Mali asked customers in late July 2024 to come to an agency with their NINA or biometric card.

Mali Tribune reports that in November 2024 the telecoms regulator AMRTP launched a national campaign to identify all mobile subscribers through their NINA number, and that Orange Mali SIMs were being registered using biometric data from the NINA card, with a 29 July 2025 APDP communique confirming complaints.
